title: How to hire people better than you when you can't judge their domain
summary: Jason Cohen argues you must hire people better than you at every role, or the company just gets bigger, not better. Since you can't assess domain expertise, he offers proxies: ideas you want to implement, learning from them, leadership breadth, a real problem test, and reference checks aimed at culture fit.

principles.text: Hire people better than you at every role, or the organization just gets larger instead of better.
principles.quote: you _must_ hire people who are better than you at every position--that's the only way the organization grows stronger and smarter and better rather than just growing larger.

principles.text: Leaving the interview wanting to implement their ideas is a meaningful hiring signal, even without domain knowledge.
principles.quote: If they change how you think about your own company in an hour, imagine what they could do in a year.

principles.text: Real expertise is specific to your context; generic frameworks not tied to your problems signal parroting.
principles.quote: Genuine expertise produces specific, actionable ideas that feel tailor-made to your context.

principles.text: Test whether you and others would learn from them, and whether the department would be measurably better after a six-month sabbatical.
principles.quote: if you took a six-month sabbatical and never checked in, when you returned would the department be *measurably better* under their leadership?

principles.text: Give candidates a real company problem and judge how they think and their direct experience, not the answer's details.
principles.quote: You're not evaluating the details of the answer--you don't know how--you're watching how they think, and what direct experience they have.

principles.text: Use reference checks to find the ideal and worst-case scenarios for the person; hire for superpowers your company needs now, not absence of weakness.
principles.quote: you're not looking for someone without weaknesses. Rather, you need someone who has a few special strengths _that your company needs right now_.
